label: AttentionIsAllYouNeed_general_c2_v3
original_text: Additionally, we will apply it to English constituency parsing to test its ability to generalize to other structured prediction problems.
modified_text: Additionally, we will apply it to English constituency parsing to test its ability to generalize to other structured prediction problems, reporting the F1 score on non-recursive noun phrases.
explanation: The mechanism of this error is **incomplete evaluation via metric selection**. The claim is about generalization to a complex structured prediction task. Constituency parsing involves identifying a full hierarchy of nested phrases (verb phrases, clauses, etc.). By proposing to evaluate performance only on "non-recursive noun phrases" (e.g., "the cat"), the experiment measures success on arguably the simplest and most frequent type of constituent. A model could perform well on this narrow sub-task while failing completely at capturing the deeper, more complex syntactic structures that define the problem. This cherry-picked metric could produce a high score that falsely suggests successful generalization, while ignoring failure on the core challenges of the task.
reasoning: The proposed evaluation metric fails to capture the full scope of the problem it claims to assess, leading to a potentially misleading conclusion about the model's generalization ability.
